    "IRES (Inverse Regression Estimation Stability): Not applicable for classification; use cross-validated classification metrics instead",

  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly distinct performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236) suggesting straighter but less directed paths or measurement floor effects",
    "Combined stimulation will show best or near-best performance: highest Success (0.780), fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), with AD highest (0.399) suggesting more exploratory or variable heading directions",
    "Bright Visual Only will outperform Dim Visual Only on Success (0.785 vs. 0.673) and Time-to-Target (2.61s vs. 3.14s), confirming luminance-dependent visual guidance",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only will perform similarly and intermediate between Sham and Combined/Bright Visual conditions",
    "ANOVAs will be highly significant given large n, but effect sizes will vary—largest effects expected for Sham comparisons, modest effects among active stimulation conditions",
    "Predictive model will achieve high accuracy distinguishing Sham from active conditions, but struggle with Combined vs. Bright Visual Only due to similar performance profiles"
  ],
  "limitations": [

    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (max=29.8) suggesting outliers or measurement artifacts that may violate ANOVA assumptions",
    "Success is trial-level binary but aggregated means suggest repeated measures; aggregation method affects variance structure",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or temporal dynamics—performance may change within sessions",
    "Single temperature setting (1.0) and specific prompt template limit generalizability of any LLM-based analysis components"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with random intercepts for Mouse, using the five performance variables as fixed-effect predictors of stimulation paradigm.
